Storm Ingrid weather warnings as UK battered by 60mph winds

Jump to content

 1. All
 2. News
 3. Sport
 4. Culture
 5. Lifestyle

 * Storm Ingrid is currently battering the UK with heavy rain and winds up to 60mph, leading to yellow weather warnings across parts of Wales, Scotland, and the south of England until Saturday morning.
 * The Met Office warns of potential flooding, travel disruption for road, rail, air, and ferry services, and the possibility of power outages due to the slow-moving system.
 * Road closures are already in place in Scotland, rail travel is affected in areas like Perth and Kincross, and three people have been rescued from stranded vehicles in Aberdeenshire.
 * The Scottish Environment Protection Agency has issued 26 flood warnings and seven flood alerts across the country.
 * Looking ahead, forecasters predict the possibility of snow in the north and east of the UK next week, with wintry conditions expected.

resultats_lens.titre: 'Thousands of trees lost' in Guernsey during Storm Goretti

brut.title: 'Thousands of trees lost' in Guernsey during Storm Goretti

webpage.text:
'Thousands of trees lost' in Guernsey during Storm Goretti

Islanders are counting the cost after Storm Goretti brought wind speeds of 95mph (154km/h) on Thursday night.

Andy McCutcheon, technical officer from Guernsey Trees for life (GTFL), said he estimated the number of trees lost in the storm was in the low thousands.

Steve Sarre, warden of Lihou island, said its house had been badly hit by the storm and the roof had been damaged. He said the damage would hit hard as Lihou was only just recovering from Storm Ciaran.

McCutcheon said the impact of the storm on the island's trees was "widespread".

"The force, the power of the storm came through was something that I think people would probably compare with the great storm of 1987," McCutcheon said.

"The final picture is going be difficult to ascertain immediately but I think over the coming days ... and I would dare to say we're probably talking low thousands," he said.

"I'm thinking this is a major event, certainly more trees came down in this storm than in the last notable storm, which is Ciaran."

McCutcheon said it might not be possible to replant in areas where large trees were lost so moving forward they would "assess each site and then work out a plan for what we're going to do in terms of species and location and numbers."


Sarre said: "Unfortunately we got hit very badly in the storm yet again. A lot of the roof is missing...and some windows smashed and things like that."

He added he thought it was going to be tough to "get back on its feet" and the house would be closed until Sunday.

But he said here had been a "great response" on Facebook from people sending messages of support.

"We've got a few people coming over that have volunteered to come and help," he added.

What is happening around Wales as nation bears the brunt of Storm Callum

Trees have been brought down, train lines closed and roads flooded

Parts of Wales will be battered by a month's rain in two days as Storm Callum lashes the nation, forecasters are warning.

Trees have been brought down, train lines closed and roads have been flooded across Wales with the fierce weather expected to continue until early on Sunday morning.

The Met Office says that high areas in south wales could see up to 200mm of rain by Sunday when the monthly total for the region is 169mm.


Traffic and travel updates here:

Here is a look at what is happening where you are in Wales:

South East Wales

The Valleys seem to be worst hit by the bad weather on Friday morning.

This was the scene on the main Heads of the Valleys road at the Rhigos Roundabout.


The road is closed and there are long tailbacks in the area.

The A4059 in Aberdare near the Tesco store is also closed because of flooding

Flooding in the Cwmbach area of Aberdare has also led to the train line closure between Fernhill and Aberdare.

Arriva Trains Wales has advised passengers not to travel as there is no road transport available either.

There are also restrictions on the M48 Severn Bridge because of high winds.

The Met Office is warning that the Valleys will be harder hit than anywhere else in the UK.


Cardiff

There is standing water - believed to be down to a blocked drain - in the Penylan area of Cardiff.

Several flights to Cardiff and Bristol airports have also been cancelled because of the bad weather. The advice is to check with your airline before you travel.

Porthcawl


The seafront has been battered by high waves.

Swansea


There is standing water on many roads including on Mumbles Road in Swansea.

Swansea promenade has also been battered by high waves.


But the bad weather didn't put off some hardy souls going in for a dip.


South West Wales

Trains from Carmarthen to Swansea were cancelled between 7am and 11am on Friday and will be suspended on Friday evening and Saturday morning because of the risk of flooding at high tide.


The Cleddau in Pembrokeshire has also been closed to high-sided vehicles.

There are several reports of fallen trees :

 * Tree blocking B4318 road at Gumfreston being cleared
 * Tree down at Lamphey Road
 * Tree at Bowett Wood, Pembroke to Hundleton road has been cleared
 * Tree down across the road at Rosepool hill on the Broadhaven to Nolton road – Crews en route
 * Tree down at Llan y cefn on the Maenchlogog road
 * Tree down across the road on the Old Whitesands Road in St Davids
 * Large Branch obstructing road at Cilwendeg between Boncath and Abercych

Mid Wales

The region is in the yellow weather warning, and has seen flooding and large coastal waves.

There have been reports of some trees being brought down in Powys, and the high tide brought large waves to the seafront at Aberystwyth.


There is also flooding at Defynnog in Powys. The A4215 has been closed between Defynnog and Libanus.

Temple Street in Llandrindod Wells has also be shut by an obstruction on the road.

North Wales

The highest wind recorded of the morning was 77mph at 7am at Capel Curig.

In north Wales, ferries and trains have already been cancelled due to the conditions and police are warning that there could be some difficult driving conditions.

One lane has also been closed in each direction on the A55 Britannia Bridge due to the high winds predicted to strike the area.


There are also trees down in Caernarfon and on Anglesey.

In Henwalia, Caernarfon , a huge trampoline was blown onto a car through the night but nobody at the scene seemed to know where it had come from.


-

webpage.text:
Warning issued ahead of 65mph winds

The Island's Met Office has issued a yellow weather warning for tomorrow (Wed 19 Sep).

The warning comes into force at 8am on Wednesday and will remain in place until 4pm.

Winds are expected to reach severe gale force, with gusts peaking at 55 to 65mph, potentially causing minor damage and travel disruption.

Motorists are warned the winds could bring down tree branches and debris on to roads.
